conventions.convention: Every table has `id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()`. Ids are normally generated client-side (UUID v4); the default is a fallback.
Trainer-scoped tables carry `trainer_id` and every query filters on it, so a wrong id answers 404, not 403.

`deleted_at` NULL means alive. Nothing is hard-deleted; every read filters `deleted_at IS NULL`. Log tables (`otp_request`, `client_assignment`, `team_activity`) have no `deleted_at` — a mistake is corrected by writing another row. Since V21 the request role holds no DELETE except on `attention_dismissal`, `web_session` and `otp_request`, and no UPDATE on the three logs.

Deleting an account is an erasure (P2), not a soft delete. `erase_account()` sets the personal columns of `app_user`, `trainer` and `client` to NULL under a CHECK that lists them, so the rows stay as tombstones, and the phone number is released. `purge_tenant()` is the one hard delete: it empties a closed workspace once `purge_after` has passed. What survives is `erasure_log`, which holds counts only, and nameless amounts and dates in workspaces the person did not own.

`updated_at` is maintained by the `set_updated_at()` trigger on every table that has it, and is the sync cursor. Since V21 there is no exception: `working_hours`, `time_block` and `batch` used to take the device's own value on sync push, which a wrong clock turned into an edit no other device ever pulled.
`tenant_id` is the workspace a row belongs to. It is stamped on insert by `stamp_tenant_id()`, refused any change by `freeze_tenant_id()`, and row-level security filters on it.
Money is `numeric(10,2)`, currency `varchar(3)` defaulting to INR, percentages `numeric(5,2)`.

Enumerated columns are plain varchar, never a Postgres ENUM. Vocabularies (profile lists, nudge kinds, `payment.method`) are validated in application code; since V21 state machines and money columns also carry a CHECK, so a new state is a code change plus one DROP / ADD CONSTRAINT in a migration. Legal values are listed per column under allowedValues.
Unless stated otherwise a foreign key is ON UPDATE NO ACTION, ON DELETE NO ACTION — rows are soft-deleted, so nothing cascades.

table.name: tenant
table.description: A workspace: the unit of isolation and the unit a customer pays for. A solo tenant is created by trigger alongside a trainer, a team tenant alongside a team.

column.name: id
column.description: Referenced as `tenant_id` by every workspace-scoped table.

column.name: type
column.description: What kind of workspace. All three kinds own rows; they differ in how many people are in them and which roles exist.

column.name: status
column.description: Switches a whole workspace off with one column.

column.name: primary_app_user_id
column.description: Who owns and pays. Not the owner of the data (that is `tenant_id` on the rows). Nullable because a gym org can exist before a person is named.

table.name: tenant_member
table.description: Who may enter a workspace, and as what. One person has one row per workspace role: a trainer who coaches privately and at a gym has two; one who is also somebody's client has a third. Team membership is mirrored into this table by trigger.

column.name: tenant_id
column.description: The workspace.

column.name: app_user_id
column.description: A person, not a trainer — a gym administrator may never coach and has no `trainer` row.

column.name: role
column.description: The owner is the admin who cannot be removed.

column.name: is_home
column.description: The workspace the app opens in. Exactly one per person.

column.name: revenue_share_percent
column.description: What this member keeps of what they collect in this workspace. NULL = 100%, the correct default for a solo tenant.

column.name: assignment_margin_percent
column.description: An admin's cut of revenue from clients they assigned to somebody else. NULL = none. Frozen per handover onto `client_assignment.actor_margin_percent`.

checks.check: (((revenue_share_percent IS NULL) OR ((revenue_share_percent >= (0)::numeric) AND (revenue_share_percent <= (100)::numeric))) AND ((assignment_margin_percent IS NULL) OR ((assignment_margin_percent >= (0)::numeric) AND (assignment_margin_percent <= (100)::numeric))))

((role)::text = ANY ((ARRAY['owner'::character varying, 'admin'::character varying, 'coach'::character varying, 'gym_admin'::character varying, 'gym_staff'::character varying, 'client'::character varying])::text[]))

index.name: uq_tenant_member_home
index.description: Exactly one home workspace per person.

index.name: uq_tenant_member_live
index.description: One live row per person per role per workspace. Two roles in one workspace is legitimate — a gym owner who also coaches.

table.name: app_user
table.description: One identity per phone number — who this number is. Deliberately thin: everything that differs by role lives in the role's own table.

column.name: phone
column.description: UNIQUE. The login. Unique product-wide, which is what makes `role` single-valued.

column.name: role
column.description: The home role: which mode sign-in opens into by default. Not exclusive — a phone can own a trainer account and also be a live client on somebody else's roster; `POST /v1/auth/mode/trainer` and `/mode/client` switch. `gym_admin` is reserved.

column.name: privacy_accepted_at
column.description: When they accepted the privacy policy. A timestamp, not a boolean: consent is evidence and evidence has a date.

table.name: otp_request
table.description: One row per sign-in code sent. Append-only and keyed by phone rather than by a user, because a code is sent before we know whether an account exists. The Postgres fallback store; Redis is the primary when enabled.

column.name: phone
column.description: No FK — deliberately: a code can be sent to a number that has no account yet.

column.name: otp_hash
column.description: Hashed, never the code.

column.name: verified
column.description: Prevents reuse of a consumed code.

column.name: wrong_attempts
column.description: Drives the max-attempts ceiling.

column.name: locked_until
column.description: The end of the wait, not its start — retuning `app.otp.lock-minutes` must not lengthen a wait someone is already serving. Persisted precisely so a restart cannot clear it.

table.name: trainer
table.description: The trainer's account and public profile: contact details, setup answers, money-book defaults and the profile a prospective client reads.

column.name: id
column.description: This is the JWT subject for a trainer token, and the `trainer_id` every other table points at.

column.name: phone
column.description: UNIQUE.

column.name: upi_vpa
column.description: Their own VPA — the app builds a UPI deep link, it never holds money.

column.name: fcm_token
column.description: Push token, written by `POST /v1/devices/token`. One token per trainer, overwritten on refresh.

column.name: experience_band
column.description: A band, never a year count.

column.name: specialities
column.description: Array of ids. Anything typed by the trainer is prefixed `custom:` and stored verbatim.

column.name: certifications
column.description: Array of ids, with `custom:` entries, like `specialities`.

column.name: languages
column.description: Array of ids, with `custom:` entries, like `specialities`. GIN-indexed — clients filter coaches by language.

column.name: setup_completed_at
column.description: The authority on whether onboarding is owed. NULL = not finished. Server-side on purpose: `isNewUser` only answers "first ever verify".

column.name: metadata
column.description: Holds `metadata.prefs` — notification switches, appearance, language, chase window, reminder tone. Preferences live here rather than in columns.

column.name: gym_name
column.description: NULL = no gym, trainer keeps 100%.

column.name: gym_share_percent
column.description: What the gym keeps of floor sessions. Remote sessions are 0% by a rule in code, not a second column.

column.name: work_mode
column.description: A hint for setup and add-client defaults; it must never gate a feature. Gym-vs-freelance is decided per client (`client.payment_mode`). NULL = never asked.

column.name: headline
column.description: One line under the name. Capped at 80 characters in `TrainerService`, not in the column; over the cap is a 400, not a truncation.

column.name: bio
column.description: 100–200 words, capped at 1200 characters in code. Also refused rather than truncated: dropping the last sentence of somebody's prose while answering 200 is the worst available outcome.

column.name: intro_video_url
column.description: A YouTube link, stored canonical — `https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=<id>`. Every share-sheet shape is reduced on write and tracking parameters are dropped. The video id rides the wire as `introVideoId`, derived not stored.

column.name: map_link
column.description: The gym or studio on a map, stored verbatim — the opposite call to `intro_video_url`, because a maps URL has no single canonical shape across Google, Apple and OSM and a normaliser would eventually break a working link. Refused over 500 characters and refused unless it is an `http(s)` URL.

column.name: training_modes
column.description: How the coaching is delivered, plus `custom:` entries. Not `work_mode` — that one is commercial and this is what a client chooses between; a gym trainer may still take home visits. GIN-indexed.

column.name: service_areas
column.description: Free-text localities the trainer travels to. Deliberately not a catalogue: no locality list would be right in two Indian cities.

column.name: instagram_url
column.description: The trainer's Instagram, stored canonical — `https://www.instagram.com/<handle>`. A bare `@handle`, a share URL with its `igsh=` token and the desktop URL all reduce to one string; a link to a post or reel is refused. Same call as `intro_video_url` and the opposite of `map_link`: a profile reduces to a handle, a place reduces to nothing. `instagramHandle` rides the wire, derived not stored.

column.name: youtube_url
column.description: The trainer's channel — not a video; `intro_video_url` is the one video they chose. Canonical `https://www.youtube.com/<@handle | channel/… | c/… | user/…>`, the path kept exactly as given because those four are not interchangeable without a lookup. A watch URL is refused with a sentence naming the field that wants it.

column.name: email
column.description: A contact detail, not a credential: nothing sends mail or verifies it, so it is stored, shown back and branched on by nothing. Deliberately neither unique nor indexed.

column.name: home_tenant_id
column.description: The trainer's own solo workspace, created alongside the trainer row by trigger.

column.name: assessment_interval_days
column.description: How often a NEW client is offered to be measured. NULL = the trainer has never said.

column.name: assessment_metrics
column.description: Which of the six measurement ids a new client's sheet holds. NULL = the product's default.

column.name: gender
column.description: Validated in `TrainerService`, not a CHECK. Clients filter on it. NULL = never asked; `undisclosed` is an answer, not an absence.

column.name: timezone
column.description: IANA zone the trainer's dates and working hours are in. Defaults to Asia/Kolkata, which every row before V21 assumed. See V21.

checks.check: (((map_link IS NULL) OR (map_link ~* '^https?://'::text)) AND ((intro_video_url IS NULL) OR (intro_video_url ~* '^https://'::text)) AND ((instagram_url IS NULL) OR (instagram_url ~* '^https://'::text)) AND ((youtube_url IS NULL) OR (youtube_url ~* '^https://'::text)))

table.name: web_session
table.description: The web's sign-in credential: an opaque, revocable session. The phone uses a self-contained JWT instead; both sit behind one issuer interface.

column.name: token_hash
column.description: UNIQUE. Hex SHA-256 of the opaque token, never the token — the same discipline as `otp_request.otp_hash`. SHA-256 and not bcrypt: this is 256 bits of `SecureRandom` with no structure to guess, so it wants a fast one-way function, not a KDF on the hot path of every authenticated request.

column.name: subject
column.description: What the equivalent JWT would carry — a trainer UUID for a trainer, the phone for every other role — so request code reads the caller identically whichever credential was presented.

column.name: tenant_id
column.description: The workspace this row belongs to.

column.name: last_seen_at
column.description: Advanced only when it has moved by more than a minute — a write per request would make this the hottest table in the schema for no accuracy anybody reads.

column.name: expires_at
column.description: `app.session.expiry-hours`, default 72. Shorter than the JWT's week on purpose: a revocable credential's lifetime is a convenience setting, not a ceiling.

column.name: revoked_at
column.description: A column rather than a DELETE, because "revoked at 14:02" is the first thing anybody wants after a security question.

column.name: user_agent
column.description: For the "signed in on" list.

table.name: subscription
table.description: The trainer's own plan and trial clock (MUST-16). One row per trainer, created by the `ensure_subscription()` trigger on trainer insert so no signup path can skip the clock. No `tenant_id` and not policied: a seat is a coaching trainer, who spans workspaces. The request role may read it and move its state; only the trigger creates a row. Never a locked door — every state still reads the money book.

column.name: trainer_id
column.description: One subscription per trainer; the trial belongs to the person who coaches, not to a workspace.

column.name: plan
column.description: `PRICING.md`'s ladder. A trial is full Pro.

column.name: state
column.description: trialing → active → past_due → grace (read-only) → free; cancelled. Moved by the provider's webhook, never by the browser redirect.

column.name: trial_started_at
column.description: When the clock started. Backfilled to `trainer.created_at` for trainers that predate V21.

column.name: trial_ends_at
column.description: Stored rather than derived, so a support extension does not rewrite when the trial began.

column.name: current_period_end
column.description: The paid period's end, from the provider.

column.name: grace_until
column.description: When read-only grace falls back to the free tier.

column.name: provider
column.description: Which rail collects: razorpay, cashfree, or manual (the hand-invoice launch posture).

column.name: provider_customer_id
column.description: The provider's customer id, from the hosted redirect. No card data ever lands in this table.

column.name: provider_mandate_id
column.description: The UPI Autopay mandate id. Unique per provider.

column.name: cancelled_at
column.description: When the trainer cancelled.

checks.check: ((provider IS NULL) OR ((provider)::text = ANY ((ARRAY['razorpay'::character varying, 'cashfree'::character varying, 'manual'::character varying])::text[])))

((state)::text = ANY ((ARRAY['trialing'::character varying, 'active'::character varying, 'past_due'::character varying, 'grace'::character varying, 'free'::character varying, 'cancelled'::character varying])::text[]))

table.name: client
table.description: A person on one trainer's roster, and the membership itself: one row has exactly one `trainer_id`. Consent is recorded on this relationship rather than in a separate membership table.

column.name: trainer_id
column.description: The owning coach. Reassignment rewrites this one column; logged history keeps its original coach. Always NOT NULL.

column.name: phone
column.description: Nullable — a trainer can keep a client with no number. When present it is how the client signs in.

column.name: status
column.description: The trainer's view of the arrangement.

column.name: trainer_split_percent
column.description: Per-client override of the gym split.

column.name: metadata
column.description: Open bag for intake questions.

column.name: weekly_schedule
column.description: `[{day:1, time:"09:00"}, …]` — the pattern auto-scheduling works from.

column.name: delivery_mode
column.description: How this client is usually trained; the default for their sessions. NULL means "nobody has said", which is what makes the per-session fallback possible.

column.name: paused_at
column.description: `status` already carries `paused`; this carries when, so the client's wall can name the date.

column.name: membership_status
column.description: The client's consent, kept separate from `status` because the two answer to different people and can disagree. New rows are written `invited` explicitly.

column.name: invited_at
column.description: When the invite was sent. It still answers "how long has this been going on" after a removal.

column.name: accepted_at
column.description: When the client accepted the invite.

column.name: removed_ack_at
column.description: When the client acknowledged the removal on their own phone. Without it the notice is permanent, because the row is kept forever for the trainer's books.

column.name: tenant_id
column.description: The workspace this row belongs to.

column.name: stale_at
column.description: Set when this client's coach has left or become unavailable in this workspace; cleared when an admin assigns a new coach. A column rather than a status, so every `status = 'active'` read keeps counting the client.

column.name: stale_reason
column.description: Why the client needs a new coach.

column.name: assigned_by_app_user_id
column.description: The admin who placed this client with their current coach, when it was a handover.

column.name: assignment_margin_percent
column.description: That admin's cut of revenue from this client, frozen at handover. NULL = none.

column.name: assigned_at
column.description: When the current coach was assigned.

column.name: assessment_interval_days
column.description: Days between measurements. NULL = this client is not on a cycle, which is a real answer and not a gap.

column.name: next_assessment_on
column.description: When the next measurement is owed. Written by the trainer; nothing advances it automatically. A date, not an instant: what is owed is a day.

column.name: assessment_metrics
column.description: This client's own sheet. NULL = whatever the trainer's default is.

column.name: date_of_birth
column.description: A date, never an age — an age is derived on read. Personal data, not health data. Refused when in the future or more than 120 years back.

checks.check: ((delivery_mode IS NULL) OR ((delivery_mode)::text = ANY ((ARRAY['floor'::character varying, 'remote'::character varying])::text[])))

(((height_cm IS NULL) OR ((height_cm >= (0)::numeric) AND (height_cm <= (300)::numeric))) AND ((sessions_per_week IS NULL) OR ((sessions_per_week >= 0) AND (sessions_per_week <= 14))) AND ((session_duration_minutes IS NULL) OR (session_duration_minutes > 0)) AND ((assessment_interval_days IS NULL) OR (assessment_interval_days > 0)))

index.name: idx_client_membership_status
index.where: (phone IS NOT NULL) AND (deleted_at IS NULL)

index.name: idx_client_next_assessment
index.where: (next_assessment_on IS NOT NULL) AND (deleted_at IS NULL)

index.name: idx_client_stale
index.where: (stale_at IS NOT NULL) AND (deleted_at IS NULL)

table.name: assessment_template
table.description: A questionnaire a trainer builds: which catalogue measurements to take and which questions to ask.

column.name: trainer_id
column.description: Every read filters on it.

column.name: name
column.description: Required.

column.name: description
column.description: Up to 2,000 characters, enforced in the service.

column.name: measurements
column.description: Catalogue keys (`AssessmentCatalogue`), filtered and de-duplicated on write.

column.name: questions
column.description: `[{id, text, kind, scale, options[], allowMultiple, allowCustom}]`, clamped on write (`API.md` → Assessments)

column.name: tenant_id
column.description: The workspace this row belongs to.

table.name: assessment
table.description: One questionnaire sent to one client: when it is due, whether it went out, and the client's readings and answers. Status is derived, never stored — `done` once completed, `booked` while unsent, `missed` once past due, otherwise `waiting`.

column.name: trainer_id
column.description: Who sent it.

column.name: template_id
column.description: `ON DELETE SET NULL`. Nulled in the same transaction when the template is soft-deleted — a sent assessment outlives its template.

column.name: name
column.description: The template's name at send time unless given.

column.name: sent_at
column.description: NULL = booked: on the board, the client has no idea.

column.name: completed_at
column.description: Set by the client's submit (portal module)

column.name: read_at
column.description: The trainer opened it; can be cleared to un-read.

column.name: measurements_asked
column.description: How many measurements were asked, frozen from the template when sent. Never negative.

column.name: questions_asked
column.description: How many questions were asked, frozen from the template when sent. Never negative.

column.name: readings
column.description: `[{key, value}]` in catalogue keys. Never copied to `body_metric` — a number the client sent back and a tape the trainer read are different claims.

column.name: answers
column.description: `[{questionId, yes, rating, text, optionIds}]`, resolved against the template's question (then the bank) on read.

column.name: tenant_id
column.description: The workspace this row belongs to.

column.name: entered_by
column.description: client | trainer — who typed the readings and answers. NULL until completed. A trainer-entered answer is never shown as the client's own. See V21 (MUST-21).

checks.check: ((entered_by IS NULL) OR ((entered_by)::text = ANY ((ARRAY['client'::character varying, 'trainer'::character varying])::text[])))

table.name: client_note
table.description: The trainer's own notes about a client — the things that do not fit a goal field: "prefers mornings, hates burpees, getting married in November".

column.name: client_id
column.description: Who the note is about.

column.name: trainer_id
column.description: Who wrote it. Stored on the row rather than reached through the client, so a team's widened reads over a teammate's client never reach that teammate's notes.

column.name: body
column.description: Free text, capped at 4,000 characters in the service; over the cap is a 400 with the reason, not a truncation.

column.name: pinned
column.description: Drawn in the always-visible strip at the top of the client's file rather than in the notes list. One flag rather than a second table: the two are prominences of one thing, and two stores would drift. Defaults false, because a strip that fills up stops being read.

column.name: tenant_id
column.description: The workspace this row belongs to.

column.name: shared_with_client
column.description: The client the note is about may read it in the portal. Teammates still never see it. Defaults to false.

table.name: team
table.description: A team of coaches. A team widens who may read a coach's clients; it never moves ownership of any row.

column.name: owner_trainer_id
column.description: Denormalised: the same fact is also a `team_member` row with `role='owner'`. Two representations bought deliberately — it answers "is this caller the owner" without a join, and it changes only inside the single transaction that transfers ownership and updates both.

column.name: logo_url
column.description: Nothing writes it yet — there is no file upload in the product.

column.name: seat_limit
column.description: NULL = unlimited. Enforced when an invite is accepted, not when it is sent: seats are consumed by people, not intentions.

column.name: tenant_id
column.description: The workspace this row belongs to.

table.name: team_member
table.description: Team membership and pending invite in one row: an invite is a membership that has not been agreed to yet.

column.name: trainer_id
column.description: Nullable, and that is the point: an invite can precede the account. A gym owner invites a coach who has never heard of InclineYou; the row is written against the phone and bound to a trainer id the first time that number signs in. This is what makes the invite an acquisition channel and not just a permission grant.

column.name: invited_phone
column.description: Kept after binding rather than cleared — it is the evidence of who was invited, and a phone on a trainer row can change afterwards.

column.name: role
column.description: The owner is not a fourth kind of admin; it is the admin who cannot be removed.

column.name: invited_at
column.description: When the invite was sent.

column.name: tenant_id
column.description: The workspace this row belongs to.

checks.check: ((trainer_id IS NOT NULL) OR (invited_phone IS NOT NULL))

index.name: uq_team_member_active_trainer
index.where: ((status)::text = 'active'::text) AND (deleted_at IS NULL) AND (trainer_id IS NOT NULL)

index.name: uq_team_member_pending_invite

table.name: client_assignment
table.description: Every reassignment of a client from one coach to another. Append-only; it is both the audit log and the source of sync tombstones for the rows that moved off the old coach's phone.

column.name: actor_trainer_id
column.description: The admin who did it, who may be neither party.

column.name: program_action
column.description: Whether the plan moved with the client.

column.name: note
column.description: Optional reason, shown to both coaches.

column.name: tenant_id
column.description: The workspace this row belongs to.

column.name: actor_margin_percent
column.description: The acting admin's cut of this client's revenue, frozen at the moment of handover. NULL = none.

column.name: reason
column.description: Why the client was moved.

table.name: team_activity
table.description: What an admin changed on a teammate's client or on the team's shared exercises. Append-only and readable by the owning coach — the trace that makes editing somebody else's plan acceptable.

column.name: actor_trainer_id
column.description: Who made the change.

column.name: subject_trainer_id
column.description: Whose data it was.

column.name: client_id
column.description: NULL for a shared custom exercise, which belongs to the team rather than to anybody's roster.

column.name: entity_id
column.description: Polymorphic — no FK, because the target is one of three tables.

column.name: summary
column.description: The sentence, written at the time, in the words the coach will read: "Changed Barbell Squat to 4 × 6 on day 2". Stored rather than derived for the same reason `weekly_report` stores its sentences — rebuilding it later would produce a different sentence every time the program changed again, which is the one thing an account of a change must not do.

column.name: tenant_id
column.description: The workspace this row belongs to.

table.name: exercise
table.description: The shared exercise library plus each trainer's custom rows, told apart by `is_custom`. Text-only: there is no image or video artwork.

column.name: muscle_group
column.description: The primary muscle, written from the same source value as `target`.

column.name: image_url
column.description: Always NULL — the library is text-only.

column.name: video_url
column.description: Always NULL — the library is text-only.

column.name: is_custom
column.description: `false` → seeded, `trainer_id` NULL. `true` → trainer-created, `trainer_id` set.

column.name: trainer_id
column.description: NULL for the shared library.

column.name: source_id
column.description: The upstream dataset's id; NOT NULL exactly when the row came from the seed.

column.name: metadata
column.description: The long tail from the seed — mechanic, category, secondary muscles.

column.name: log_type
column.description: How a set of it is logged — `weight_reps` (a load and a count), `reps` (a count, bodyweight) or `time` (a hold or an interval, in seconds: a plank, a wall sit, a dead hang). Set once when a custom exercise is created and then immutable — every set already recorded against it would stop making sense. NULL reads as `weight_reps`. `time` added 25 Sep 2026: without it a plank could only be prescribed as reps.

column.name: body_part
column.description: Ten values (back, cardio, chest, lower arms, lower legs, neck, shoulders, upper arms, upper legs, waist). How a trainer scans a library, so it is what the list groups by.

column.name: target
column.description: Nineteen values (abs, biceps, lats, quads, …). Finer than `body_part`; what the muscle filter offers. On a custom row, its primary muscle.

column.name: tenant_id
column.description: The workspace this row belongs to.

column.name: status
column.description: Drafts exist only on custom rows and are hidden from the default library read and from `/categories`.

column.name: secondary_targets
column.description: List of muscles worked besides `target`. Unseeded. NULL reads as `[]`.

column.name: form_cues
column.description: List of short coaching cues. Deliberately unseeded — a generated cue served as real is a coaching instruction nobody wrote; filling it is an authored content pass. NULL reads as `[]`.

checks.check: (is_custom OR ((image_url IS NULL) AND (video_url IS NULL)))
((log_type IS NULL) OR ((log_type)::text = ANY ((ARRAY['weight_reps'::character varying, 'reps'::character varying, 'time'::character varying])::text[])))
(((image_url IS NULL) OR (image_url ~* '^https?://'::text)) AND ((video_url IS NULL) OR (video_url ~* '^https?://'::text)))

column.description: The workspace this row belongs to.

table.name: template
table.description: A trainer's reusable program blueprint. Its days are ordinal slots (Day 1…Day 7); weekdays and times are chosen per client when it is applied.

column.name: structure
column.description: The exercise blueprint, including timed prescriptions and the named-workout keys `workout_id` / `workout_name`.

column.name: day_labels
column.description: `{"1":"Push Day","3":"Pull Day"}`.

column.name: weeks
column.description: Program length, which is what the weeks × days matrix is drawn from. NULL reads as one week.

column.name: training_days
column.description: Ordinal day slots as CSV, `"1,3,5"` — Day 1…Day 7, not weekdays. NULL reads as "not told" and the reader falls back to whichever days the blueprint uses.

column.name: tenant_id
column.description: The workspace this row belongs to.

column.name: source
column.description: `own` on every row — a copy of a certified program is the trainer's own.

column.name: copied_from_id
column.description: `ON DELETE SET NULL` — the one FK in the schema that declares an ON DELETE. Certified rows are soft-deleted, so it should never fire.

column.name: copied_from_name
column.description: The original's name as at copy time, so a copy can still name it after it is retired.

column.name: copied_from_updated_at
column.description: The original's `updated_at` at copy time. Older than the original's current one means the original has been revised since. Nothing propagates.

index.name: idx_template_copied_from
index.where: (copied_from_id IS NOT NULL) AND (deleted_at IS NULL)

table.name: certified_template
table.description: Programs InclineYou authors: a catalogue readable from every workspace and writable by no request. A trainer copies one into `template` and the copy is theirs. It carries no `tenant_id`.

column.name: goal
column.description: Copied onto the trainer's template.

column.name: description
column.description: Copied onto the trainer's template.

column.name: summary
column.description: The shelf card's sentence.

column.name: structure
column.description: The blueprint, shaped like `template.structure`, except each entry names its movement by `exercise_source_id` (the library's stable source key) rather than `exercise_id`, and is resolved to `exercise.id` on read and on copy. An unresolvable entry is dropped.

column.name: day_labels
column.description: `{"1":"Upper A", …}` — ordinal slots, like a template's.

column.name: training_days
column.description: Ordinal slots, CSV.

column.name: reviewed_at
column.description: When a qualified human reviewed the program — not `updated_at`. NULL = never reviewed.

column.name: is_sample
column.description: A placeholder written to exercise the shelf, not authored content. Both current rows are samples.

column.name: used_count
column.description: How many copies have been made. Moves only through `certified_template_used(uuid)`; never negative.

table.name: program
table.description: One client's plan: an independent copy of a template (or built from scratch), laid onto that client's chosen weekdays and times.

column.name: trainer_id
column.description: Moves on reassignment.

column.name: template_id
column.description: Provenance only — the exercises are an independent copy, and the template may have been deleted since.

column.name: schedule
column.description: The client's chosen layout: which weekday each ordinal template day lands on, and at what time — `[{"day":1,"weekday":2,"time":"06:30"}, …]`. Written by `POST /v1/templates/{id}/apply`; the count must match the template's day count. NULL on programs built directly on weekdays.

column.name: tenant_id
column.description: The workspace this row belongs to.

column.name: day_labels
column.description: The copy's own day names, keyed by WEEKDAY (`{"2":"Push"}`) where `template.day_labels` is keyed by ordinal slot. Re-keyed through `schedule` at apply and at resync — copying them verbatim would put the blueprint's name for slot 3 on a Wednesday the client never trains.

column.name: weeks
column.description: How long THIS client's block runs. Taken from the template at apply and editable per client — nine weeks of an eight-week blueprint is a per-client decision.

column.name: training_days
column.description: CSV of the weekdays this client trains, the same encoding `template.training_days` uses for ordinal slots. `TemplateService.parseDayCsv`/`dayCsv` is the one parser for both.

column.name: synced_at
column.description: When this copy last took the blueprint — on apply and on resync, nothing else. `updated_at` cannot answer that, because editing the copy moves it.

table.name: program_exercise
table.description: The prescription: one exercise on one day of one week of a client's program. Reaches its coach through `program_id`; it has no `trainer_id`.

column.name: reps
column.description: A count. A hold goes in `duration_seconds`, never here.

column.name: day_of_week
column.description: 1 (Mon) – 7 (Sun); NULL = unscheduled.

column.name: order_index
column.description: The plan's order. It must not move because one morning ran backwards — that is `workout_exercise.order_index`'s job.

column.name: week
column.description: Which week of the program. NULL reads as week 1.

column.name: duration_seconds
column.description: For a timed exercise — "3 × 45s plank". Set instead of `reps`; writing 45 into `reps` would lie to everything that reads reps as a count.

column.name: tempo
column.description: Lifting tempo, free text.

column.name: alt_exercise_id
column.description: An approved alternative the client may swap to on the day.

column.name: group_id
column.description: A correlation id shared by the adjacent members of one superset — not a foreign key, and minted per program.

column.name: set_detail
column.description: One object per set, `{reps, durationSeconds, toFailure}`, present only when the sets differ from each other. While they agree, `sets` and `reps` say it and this is NULL.

column.name: tenant_id
column.description: The workspace this row belongs to.

column.name: workout_id
column.description: Which named workout block on its day this row belongs to. A local handle, not a foreign key, so unindexed. NULL = the day's single unnamed block.

column.name: workout_name
column.description: The block's name ("Upper A"), copied from the blueprint by apply and resync.

checks.check: (((week IS NULL) OR (week >= 0)) AND ((sets IS NULL) OR (sets >= 0)) AND ((reps IS NULL) OR (reps >= 0)) AND ((rest_seconds IS NULL) OR (rest_seconds >= 0)) AND ((duration_seconds IS NULL) OR (duration_seconds >= 0)) AND ((target_load IS NULL) OR (target_load >= (0)::numeric)))

index.name: idx_program_exercise_group
index.where: (group_id IS NOT NULL) AND (deleted_at IS NULL)

table.name: workout_template
table.description: A trainer's saved single workout ("Upper A"), prescribed set by set, which can be poured into any program day. Web-only; never synced.

column.name: trainer_id
column.description: The owner; every read filters on it.

column.name: name
column.description: Defaults to "New workout" in the service.

column.name: notes
column.description: Up to 500 characters, enforced in the service.

column.name: exercises
column.description: `[{id, exerciseId, orderIndex, groupId, alternatives:[{exerciseId, sets}], sets:[{loadKind, loadValue, effortKind, effortValue, restSeconds, tempo, notes}]}]` — camelCase, the wire's own shape. Normalised on every write; every `exerciseId` is checked against the caller's library. Replaced whole by PUT.

column.name: dividers
column.description: `[{label, beforeIndex}]` headings, clamped to `[0, exercises.length]` and sorted.

column.name: tenant_id
column.description: The workspace this row belongs to.

table.name: scheduled_session
table.description: A calendar entry in the trainer's diary: one client (or one batch attendee) at one time on one day.

column.name: trainer_id
column.description: Moves on reassignment.

column.name: status
column.description: Capped at four on purpose — every status is a decision someone has to make mid-session. Confirmation and cancellation-attribution are separate columns rather than a fifth and sixth status.

column.name: day_label
column.description: Denormalised from the template for fast list display.

column.name: template_day
column.description: Which program day's exercises to pre-populate the log with.

column.name: delivery_mode
column.description: Per-session override of `client.delivery_mode`. A floor client's Thursday check-in call is remote, and that is the case the home-screen chips exist to make visible.

column.name: series_id
column.description: Recurrence. No FK — this is not a table: the occurrences are real rows created together, not a rule evaluated at read time, and this is what lets "cancel the rest of these" find them. NULL for a one-off.

column.name: cancelled_by
column.description: The two kinds of cancellation differ in who apologises, not in what the diary shows.

column.name: pack_delta
column.description: The pack ledger, inlined. A pack moves on `done` or `no_show`, never on booking, and every such change is undoable for 24 hours — so undo has to know exactly what was applied and to which package, because by then the package may have been renewed, part-paid or expired.

column.name: pack_package_id
column.description: Which package was moved. No FK constraint — it is a remembered pointer for undo, not a live relationship.

column.name: moved_from_at
column.description: Set when the trainer moves a booking, cleared never. A timestamp rather than a boolean so the client's notice can strike the old time through — a client shown only the new time cannot tell what changed and will ask, which is the WhatsApp exchange the notice exists to replace.

column.name: client_confirmed_at
column.description: The client's one-tap confirm. A confirmed session is still `scheduled`. This is the only thing a client may write to this table — they cannot move, cancel or no-show, because all three change somebody else's working day.

column.name: batch_id
column.description: Every attendee keeps their own row and they share a batch.

column.name: tenant_id
column.description: The workspace this row belongs to.

column.name: from_schedule
column.description: TRUE when the diary laid this row down from the client's standing week, and may therefore move or remove it. NULL or FALSE means a trainer booked or moved it by hand and it is left alone.

checks.check: ((cancelled_by IS NULL) OR ((cancelled_by)::text = ANY ((ARRAY['client'::character varying, 'trainer'::character varying])::text[])))
((delivery_mode IS NULL) OR ((delivery_mode)::text = ANY ((ARRAY['floor'::character varying, 'remote'::character varying])::text[])))

index.name: idx_scheduled_session_batch
index.where: (batch_id IS NOT NULL) AND (deleted_at IS NULL)

index.name: idx_scheduled_session_delivery_mode
index.where: (delivery_mode IS NOT NULL) AND (deleted_at IS NULL)

index.name: idx_scheduled_session_program
index.where: (program_id IS NOT NULL) AND (deleted_at IS NULL)

index.name: idx_scheduled_session_series
index.where: (series_id IS NOT NULL) AND (deleted_at IS NULL)

table.name: working_hours
table.description: When the trainer works: one row per window, not per day, because a split shift (06:00–11:00 and 17:00–21:00) is two windows.

column.name: weekday
column.description: 0 = Monday … 6 = Sunday, ISO order to match the day strip. Note this differs from `program_exercise.day_of_week`, which is 1–7.

column.name: start_minute
column.description: Minutes from midnight, not `TIME`: every consumer does interval arithmetic on it, and a free-slot search is subtraction — done on the phone, where SQL time types buy nothing.

column.name: tenant_id
column.description: The workspace this row belongs to.

table.name: time_block
table.description: A dated hole in the diary — an afternoon off or a fortnight away. It stops new bookings and nothing else; sessions already inside it stay where they are.

column.name: all_day
column.description: Explicit, so a viewer never has to infer it from 00:00–23:59.

column.name: tenant_id
column.description: The workspace this row belongs to.

table.name: batch
table.description: A group session on the floor: several clients in one slot. Each attendee keeps their own `scheduled_session` row pointing here.

column.name: capacity
column.description: What the floor holds; the diary's "8/10" is booked over this.

column.name: min_size
column.description: Below this it is not worth running, and the agenda row says so in advance while there is still time to fill it.

column.name: tenant_id
column.description: The workspace this row belongs to.

table.name: workout_session
table.description: A session that actually happened and was logged, booked or not.

column.name: trainer_id
column.description: Does not move on reassignment — a logged session keeps its original coach.

column.name: scheduled_session_id
column.description: Nullable: a session can be logged that was never booked.

column.name: session_date
column.description: A calendar day, not an instant.

column.name: ended_at
column.description: When the log was closed — a different fact from whether the session counts against a pack (`scheduled_session.status` carries that). NULL is read as "still open".

column.name: tenant_id
column.description: The workspace this row belongs to.

index.name: idx_workout_session_scheduled
index.where: (scheduled_session_id IS NOT NULL) AND (deleted_at IS NULL)

table.name: workout_exercise
table.description: What is in today's log, in today's order: exercises added before their first set, planned ones swapped out, and the order they were dragged into — facts about today, not edits to the program.

column.name: order_index
column.description: Today's order. Starts as the plan's and diverges the moment somebody drags a card.

column.name: source
column.description: An unplanned exercise is a first-class row — same card, same table, counted in volume, one quiet tag. This column draws that tag and nothing else: it is not a quality mark and adherence must never read it.

column.name: swapped_from_exercise_id
column.description: Set when this row replaced a planned exercise. The rack was busy; the bench press was not skipped, it was swapped — and that distinction is the most important thing this table records. Adherence reads this, not the absence of the original.

column.name: target_sets
column.description: Copied from the plan when the log opened, not joined — editing the plan next week must not rewrite what happened today.

column.name: rest_seconds
column.description: Per-exercise, never global: 90s after a bench set and 20s after a curl is one trainer, not two preferences. NULL means the plan's value.

column.name: removed_at
column.description: Taken out of today. Separate from `deleted_at`: the row is still the record that the trainer decided not to do this, and the toast's Undo needs something to put back. `deleted_at` is for a row that should never have existed.

column.name: tenant_id
column.description: The workspace this row belongs to.

checks.check: (((target_sets IS NULL) OR (target_sets >= 0)) AND ((target_reps IS NULL) OR (target_reps >= 0)) AND ((rest_seconds IS NULL) OR (rest_seconds >= 0)))

table.name: set_log
table.description: The individual sets logged within a workout session.

column.name: exercise_id
column.description: Points at the exercise directly rather than at `workout_exercise`.

column.name: rpe
column.description: 1–10, one decimal place.

column.name: tenant_id
column.description: The workspace this row belongs to.

checks.check: ((set_number >= 0) AND ((reps IS NULL) OR (reps >= 0)) AND ((load_kg IS NULL) OR (load_kg >= (0)::numeric)) AND ((rpe IS NULL) OR ((rpe >= (0)::numeric) AND (rpe <= 10.5))))

table.name: pack
table.description: The price list — what a trainer sells. Distinct from `package`, which is one of these sold to one client: a menu versus a bill.

column.name: sessions
column.description: NULL for a monthly pack, which is a duration and not a count.

column.name: validity_days
column.description: NULL = no expiry, which is what most Indian trainers actually run.

column.name: status
column.description: Retiring is `inactive`: the pack stops being offered and every package sold from it stays exactly as it was. Never deleted while a package points at it.

column.name: order_index
column.description: The trainer's own ordering, not a sort key we invent.

column.name: owner
column.description: A trainer employed at a gym sells two different things: their own packs, which they price and can discount, and the gym counter's packages, which they can do neither to. One column rather than a second table every price-list read would have to union.

column.name: tenant_id
column.description: The workspace this row belongs to.

table.name: package
table.description: One pack sold to one client: sessions or a month, what it cost, what is still owed, and its pause / expiry lifecycle.

column.name: trainer_id
column.description: Does not move on reassignment.

column.name: sessions_remaining
column.description: Decremented when a session is marked `done` — see `scheduled_session.pack_delta` for the undo trail.

column.name: amount
column.description: Already net. It is what this client owes; `discount_amount` only records why it is lower than the list price.

column.name: status
column.description: A package closes to `completed` when its sessions run out and to `expired` when its validity lapses. Read `amountDue > 0`, not `status = 'active'`, to find packs with money on them.

column.name: pack_id
column.description: The price-list entry it was sold from. Nullable: a package can be sold without one.

column.name: due_date
column.description: Without it there is no such thing as "11 days late", and chasing is the highest-value job on the Money screen. NULL means never agreed, which reads as "due, not late".

column.name: written_off_at
column.description: A write-off is not a delete: the debt stays visible in the client's book and in the year's written-off total, it just stops being chased.

column.name: written_off_amount
column.description: Stored separately from `amount`, which is what keeps both figures true when a client paid ₹2,000 of ₹6,000 and the rest was let go.

column.name: discount_amount
column.description: Lands on the sold package, not on the pack: a discount is given to one client on one sale, and putting it on the price list would re-quote everybody else.

column.name: paused_at
column.description: When the current pause began; NULL = running. A column rather than a status, so every `status = 'active'` read keeps counting a client who is on holiday. The one thing it gates is the charge when a session is marked done.

column.name: paused_days
column.description: Total days lost to pauses, each added onto `end_date` on resume, so the expiry date can show its working.

column.name: closed_at
column.description: When the lifecycle sweep moved the package off `active`.

column.name: tenant_id
column.description: The workspace this row belongs to.

checks.check: (((sessions_total IS NULL) OR (sessions_total >= 0)) AND ((sessions_remaining IS NULL) OR (sessions_remaining >= 0)))
((status)::text = ANY ((ARRAY['active'::character varying, 'completed'::character varying, 'expired'::character varying, 'cancelled'::character varying, 'refunded'::character varying])::text[]))

table.name: package_adjustment
table.description: What has happened to a sold pack — pause, resume, extend, or a session-count correction. Append-only in practice.

column.name: days
column.description: Signed. The pause's length on a `resume`, the goodwill given on an `extend`, `0` on a `pause` (an open pause has no length yet) and `0` on a correction.

column.name: reason
column.description: Free text, never parsed. Offered and never demanded: a required field between a trainer on a gym floor and a two-second kindness is a field that stops the kindness.

column.name: effective_at
column.description: Back-datable — trainers catch up on Sundays, and a pause dated to the Thursday the client actually left returns the right number of days.

column.name: tenant_id
column.description: The workspace this row belongs to.

column.name: sessions
column.description: Signed change to `sessions_total` made by a correction. `0` on the three verbs that move days. Never written by a sale — buying more sessions is a second `package` row, because a package is what one client bought and editing it would rewrite the agreement.

table.name: payment
table.description: Money coming in: a client paying a trainer, against a package. A collected payment is `paid` or `confirmed`.

column.name: trainer_id
column.description: Does not move on reassignment.

column.name: client_id
column.description: `NOT NULL`, which is exactly why a gym settlement could not be a row in this table.

column.name: status
column.description: `confirmed` arrives through sync and counts as collected, like `paid`. A written-off row keeps its amount and adds it to `package.written_off_amount`.

column.name: gym_share_amount
column.description: The gym's cut, applied at record time and stored on the row.

column.name: share_percent
column.description: Copied onto the row, never looked up later: if the contract changes from 50% to 40% in October, September's split must not move.

column.name: receipt_no
column.description: Issued on the device, from a device-scoped range, because cash arrives in basements with no signal. Two phones must never mint the same number.

column.name: note
column.description: "He paid the rest in cash on Tuesday." Free text, never parsed. A write-off's reason is appended as `"<old> · <reason>"`.

column.name: tenant_id
column.description: The workspace this row belongs to.

column.name: invoice_no

column.name: invoiced_at
column.description: When the number was minted.

checks.check: ((status)::text = ANY ((ARRAY['pending'::character varying, 'paid'::character varying, 'confirmed'::character varying, 'overdue'::character varying, 'write_off'::character varying])::text[]))
